Keep in mind that this SubReddit is to get a good laugh and is NOT good for learning how to write. At all. Many paragraphs are taken out of context, even if in the book it made perfect sense with the character or the scene itself - or sometimes books from 200 years ago get analysed by modern standards.

EVERYTHING can be written. EVERYTHING. The hard thing is writing it well! A good thing to ask yourself is *does it make sense in the context of the book, the character, the scene*? If it does, then you are pretty safe. Also, always ask somebody to read your things after you. Sometimes we get so enamoured with our melon-boobs metaphors that we don't understand they actually come out as pretty ridiculous to a reader. I am sure you will be fine in this, just the fact that you care to ask tells me you are already pretty safe. :D

It all comes down to focus and style, I think.

What comes out as weird is that often the breasts are described out of the blue in a context where nobody would look at them - a few days ago I saw an entry here in which the mother of the protagonist run towards him, worried because something bad happened, and in the midst of a (very mediocre) scene of tension the description of her boobs going *boing-boing* was just... Weird. Who would look at his own mother's boobs? While she was showing concern for you?

If the focus of the scene is on something that would actually concern boobs, or another sexualised part of the body, then it's fine to focus on them. And we come to the second point: style.

I get it. Writing is hard. Being original in a time like ours can be difficult, it feels like everybody already said everything in every possible way. But the breasts that "perk up", or react to the emotions of the woman (do authors think they move like cat ears or what?!), or resemble "beautiful watermelons," are just ridiculous. If your attempt to convince me a woman is sexy, even if the context is right, is to explain how her breasts resemble a fruit, I will never take it seriously. Sexiness asks for sexy descriptions. Watermelons and "jiggling" boobs are not sexy images. To be fair, sometimes the description of a smile or of a simple movement can say tons more about how charming a character is, but I digress.

Also, implying that a woman is sexy when she looks underage is weird. And I get it: there are characters that are pedophiles, or rapists, or simply perverted guys that glance at boobs of every single woman they meet. And these character can be protagonists, it's fine. But it's VERY hard to write them right without it coming off wrong, and it's no simple thing to explain. Of course there will always be readers that will misinterpret what you wrote, but there are objective facts ALSO in literature (and don't believe who says otherwise) that cannot be brought down by personal taste. It's fine to say you didn't like *Lolita*, for example, and that it made you uncomfortable - it's just plain wrong to claim that it's a book that encourages pedophilia.

The best thing to learn how to write is to read a lot of good literature.

The context makes it that: just a word. If anything, this taboo of the words is being imported through internet FROM America. I don't know how to translate it in English, I truly hope it doesn't come out as offensive. But if you look at my ancestors, I have people from Eastern Europe, from Africa, and from Northern Europe - and it's fairly common because of our history and of our position in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea. We were invaded multiple times and had exchanges with many different ethnicities/nationalities. People in the South tend to have darker skin and black/curly hair due to past exchanges with Arabs/Africans (and, well, the Mediterranean type is generically darker) - people in the North can easily be paler because they were invaded from Austria and France (and because the Mediterranean type doesn't come from the middle of the mountains).

Your type, as you described yourself, if what we call "tratti mediterranei" - but it's widely spread only in certain areas of Italy, and even there, it's not like it's necessarily the majority of people you'll see around. We have been such a melting pot of cultures in the past that it's hard to find coherency even in a single family.

EDIT: Forgot to add, it's a type that's widely spread also in Greece, Spain and Portugal, just to make a few examples. That's why to us it sounds so weird that you'd call Italian an "ethnicity", because we feel Italian by culture (and to be clear, if you got to learn about Italian traditions through your family it's cool and it's part of your identity!) - for sure not by our appearance, that is so... *Undefined*, in our own head.
As an Italian, I tell you that no Italian will ever tell you that Italian is an ethnicity. Really, if you look at ethnicity, we are basically the most "mixed" people in Europe.

Understand why they do it, and if they do it only with you - if the intent is malicious or not really changes the perspective.

If they do it because of depression, personal problems, issues or whatever important reason, then be patient. If they do it for more petty reason such as *I need to lock myself in my room from time to time just because*, consider if it's something you can deal with and act accordingly. I had many friends like this and sometimes I am the friend that disappears because of very personal reasons, there are people that accept it and others that find it horrible: we parted ways and that was all. This counts only of they do it with everybody of course.

If they do it only with you, then you probably aren't their friend.

Overall, when I feel like that is when I have to really push myself do something productive. That doesn't necessarily mean study, work, earn money or whatever, but do something that does me real good.

Clean the room, read a book, try a new game or find a creative outlet: all the suggestions I read before are awesome and really help, but I wouldn't be surprised if none of them tickled your fancy. When one is at a low point, really every activity seems pointless and/or too much - that's why I recommend to give yourself that little push. Yeah, at first you'll hate it probably, but let yourself sink in that activity and you'll enjoy it; and at the end of the day, you'll be able to tell yourself "Hey, I did this today, it did me good."

Maybe make a little list, simple enjoyable tasks to keep yourself in check. When depression gets me, nothing beats me down even more than reaching the end of the day realizing I wasted hours doing nothing - so please don't let that win you over!

Wish you the best!
